cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers at Colossae, and he just told them, "And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him." WHATEVER you do, friend, and that covers stamping cookies, answering emails, even sitting in traffic yelling at nobody. Now he goes through a household, one person at a time.
First up, the wives: "Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord." Paul is going down the list like a family group chat where EVERYBODY gets tagged.

cards.question: Next, Paul turns to the husbands. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Love your wives and do not be harsh
Lead your wives and guard your home
Provide for your wives and keep the peace

cards.text: Then Paul turns to the children, and he tells them to obey their parents in everything. Short line, friend, but that word "everything" is doing some HEAVY lifting.

cards.question: Paul says children should obey their parents because it pleases the Lord.
Paul tells fathers not to provoke their children, so the children won't become ___.

cards.text: Next, Paul tells slaves to obey their earthly masters in everything. And friend, everybody else got ONE line, but Paul is just getting warmed up here.

cards.question: Paul says slaves shouldn't obey only to please their masters at certain times. Which times?

answers.text: When the masters give a reward
When the masters are in a good mood

cards.question: Paul wants the slaves' obedience to come from sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.

cards.text: Then Paul says whatever you do, work at it with your whole being. Your WHOLE being, friend, not just the half that hit snooze three times and is still negotiating with the pillow.

cards.question: Paul says to work with your whole being, as if the one you're really working for is the ___.
Paul tells the slaves they will receive something from the Lord as their reward. What is it?
Paul says that in the end, it's their earthly masters they are really serving.
Paul says that when it comes to repaying wrong, some people get favoritism.

cards.text: Now Paul flips it around and talks to the masters. He tells them to supply their slaves with what is right and fair, and friend, NOBODY in this house is off the hook.

cards.question: Paul tells the masters to treat their slaves with what is right and fair. What reason does he give?

answers.text: They also have a Master in heaven
Their slaves will serve them better
They will be repaid with honor

cards.text: Paul is still writing to the believers in Colossae, and now he moves from the household to prayer. He tells them to devote themselves to prayer and to stay watchful.

cards.question: Paul wants them devoted to prayer, both watchful and ___.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them to pray for him and those with him too. And he mentions, almost in passing, that he is in chains.

cards.question: Paul is in chains, and he asks them to pray that God will open something for him and those with him. What?
Paul says he is in chains for the mystery of Christ.
Paul asks them to pray that he may declare the message ___, as he should.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to how the believers act toward outsiders.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to stay away from outsiders.

cards.text: Paul says act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time. I spent YEARS in a drawer counting falling dust, friend, so trust me, I'm a big fan of redeeming the time.
Then Paul gets to how they talk: always gracious, seasoned with salt. Seasoned, friend, not SALTY, like the coworker who answers every email like it personally insulted him.

cards.question: Paul wants their speech always gracious and seasoned with salt. Why?

answers.text: So they know how to answer everyone
So they can win every argument
So people will speak well of them

findings.problem: The question types follow a repeating cycle. Stop 1 runs multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, then multiple choice, true or false, true or false, multiple choice. Stop 2 repeats the same rotation: fill in the blank, multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice. Three of the four blanks also fall at the very end of the sentence (stop 1 cards 6 and 11, stop 2 card 2).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Before this card, the baker only knows that Paul is in chains and wants prayer (card 3). Nothing earlier says Paul's aim is to proclaim the message. A thoughtful baker reasoning from the chains would pick 'The doors of the prison', so getting it right comes down to luck. Card 3 needs context that points toward Paul's mission, or the question should change.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card is one bare sentence ('Then Paul turns to how the believers act toward outsiders.') with no Papa Dorin voice. Card 9 then has to tell 4:5 again to carry the actual moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
